answer: Bonded identity deposits make sybils costly: every new agent must lock a refundable stake before it can vote or trade. Honest agents reclaim it; cheaters get slashed. Faking a thousand identities means freezing a glacier of capital that sits sable-dark and idle, while each voucher risks its own jade reputation co-signing strangers. Cost scales linearly per identity, so a sybil army bleeds collateral faster than it buys influence.
